title: [source-facebook-marketing] Unable to parse access token
body: I am using source-facebook-marketing 3.3.6 in Airbyte Cloud. Since the selectable-auth change, I can no longer edit or create Facebook Marketing sources using Airbyte's authentication flow with a secretId. Editing an existing source or creating one in the UI fails with “Invalid OAuth access token - Cannot parse access token.” Creating one through the Cloud API fails with “Missing param auth_type,” although that parameter does not appear in the API documentation. I authenticate Airbyte and add an account ID rather than supplying my own access token.

symptoms_visible: Editing an existing Facebook Marketing source or creating a new one in Airbyte Cloud fails with “Invalid OAuth access token - Cannot parse access token.”
Creating the source through the Cloud API with a secretId fails with “Missing param auth_type.”
N0.label: N0 managed OAuth source creation failures reported

symptoms_visible: The same UI and API errors remain, and I do not have a personal access token, client ID, or client secret to put into the source because I use Airbyte's secretId flow.
N0_x.label: N0_x manual OAuth credentials direction rejected

symptoms_visible: The example source no longer passes Test and Save, and the connection using it no longer syncs.
N1.label: N1 affected Cloud resources identified

symptoms_visible: My existing Facebook Marketing connections continue to run, while sources I edit or newly create with Airbyte authentication fail.
The Cloud API also fails when I submit the secret_id returned by Airbyte's browser flow.
N1_x.label: N1_x Facebook account explanation contradicted

symptoms_visible: My existing Facebook Marketing connections continue to run, while edited and newly created sources using Airbyte authentication fail.
The managed authentication dialog completes, but setting up the source afterward still produces the access-token parsing error.
N2.label: N2 Airbyte-managed application flow confirmed

symptoms_visible: The recordings reproduce a new-source failure, a secretId Cloud API request failure, and an unchanged existing source failing immediately at Test and Save.
N3.label: N3 failures reproduced in private recordings

symptoms_visible: The same Cloud UI setup succeeds without an error in a different browser or an incognito session.
Creating the source through the Cloud API succeeds when I send credentials.auth_type as Client alongside secretId.
N_terminal.label: terminal managed OAuth source creation working

solution.intent: Replace the managed secretId flow with manually supplied OAuth credentials, including an access token, client ID, client secret, and Client authentication type.
solution.concrete_example: Populate credentials with auth_type set to Client and directly provide an access token, client ID, and client secret.

edges.comment: From c1-c2, on RocketerJames's setup: a maintainer proposed a normal manually supplied OAuth credential object, but the reporter explained that he uses Airbyte's secretId flow and does not possess or pass those credentials.

edges.comment: Recovery from the rejected c1 credential advice into c3-c4: the same reporter identifies the affected Airbyte Cloud resources without changing his managed-auth configuration.

solution.intent: Treat the invalid-token response as a Facebook account or account-ID problem and refer the reporter to Facebook Support.
solution.concrete_example: Ask Facebook Support to investigate the account and account ID because the OAuthException comes from Facebook.

edges.comment: From c10-c11, on RocketerJames's system: the maintainer attributed the OAuthException to Facebook, but the reporter countered that existing connections still ran and only edited or newly created Airbyte-managed-auth sources failed, including through the Cloud API.

question_patterns: Whose Facebook application is involved, and do you generate or store the OAuth tokens yourself?
Can you confirm whether this uses your own Facebook app or an application managed by Airbyte?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The app belongs to Airbyte. I do not pass my own authentication credentials, generate the tokens, or store them; Airbyte's Facebook app acts on my behalf through the browser flow and gives me a secret_id for the API.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It is my own Facebook app, and I manually generate and store its access token, client ID, and client secret.
It is still Airbyte's app, but I initiated the browser flow from another workstation.

question_patterns: What do you see when you authenticate the Facebook Marketing account from the Cloud UI?
Can you show the authentication screen presented while creating a new source?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I click “Authenticate your Facebook Marketing account” while setting up a new source, I get this Airbyte Cloud authentication screen. Authentication appears to complete, but clicking Set up source afterward fails.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The authentication dialog uses a different window size, but the same steps and failure occur.

edges.comment: From c10-c15, on RocketerJames's managed Cloud flow: before answering the app-ownership question, the reporter volunteered that existing connections continued running while only edited and newly created managed-auth sources failed, contradicting the Facebook-account direction. He then clarified that the app, credentials, and tokens are controlled by Airbyte and supplied screenshots of the browser and Cloud UI flow.

question_patterns: Whose Facebook application and credentials are used by this browser flow?
Do you manage the Facebook app and tokens yourself?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The app belongs to Airbyte. I do not provide, generate, or store the OAuth credentials; Airbyte's browser flow returns the secret_id that I pass to the Cloud API.

question_patterns: What happens during the Cloud UI authentication step?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Airbyte authentication dialog is presented and appears to complete, but the source fails when I click Set up source.

edges.comment: Recovery from c10-c11 into c12-c15, still describing RocketerJames's deployment: the reporter distinguishes Airbyte-managed OAuth from a Facebook account or customer-owned application problem. The two screenshots are attached only on the canonical N1-to-N2 edge.

question_patterns: Can you record the complete steps from starting authentication through the failure?
Could you privately share recordings of the UI and API failures so we can reproduce the same sequence?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I sent three screencast links through support ticket 6993: one shows a new source failing from scratch, one shows the documented curl request with the secretId failing, and one shows an otherwise functional connection's source failing immediately when I edit nothing and click Test and Save.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The recordings do not reproduce the issue; all three source setup paths succeed when recorded.
I sent the same three recordings through a different private support channel.

edges.comment: From c16-c20, solely on RocketerJames's setup: the maintainer requested a private end-to-end recording, and the reporter sent three recordings through the existing support ticket. No unavailable private recording is referenced as an image.

solution.intent: Restore the Airbyte-managed OAuth setup by retrying the Cloud UI flow in a clean browser context and, for Cloud API creation with secretId, including the required Client authentication discriminator in the credentials object.
solution.concrete_example: Retry the same Cloud UI authentication and source setup in another browser or an incognito window. For the Cloud API request, keep the secretId flow and include "credentials":{"auth_type":"Client"}; then verify that source creation and Test and Save succeed.
solution.inference_hint: The thread does not establish a deeper browser-cache or connector-migration mechanism. It only establishes that the identical UI process succeeds in another browser or incognito session and that the Cloud API accepts the managed secretId request when credentials.auth_type is Client. Do not overstate the root cause beyond those observed requirements.

edges.comment: Resolution from c22, on RocketerJames's own system: before the maintainer reviewed the recordings, the reporter independently confirmed that a different browser/incognito fixed the UI path and that adding credentials.auth_type=Client alongside secretId fixed Cloud API creation. Both successful outcomes are introduced at the terminal node.

satisfaction_conditions: Must preserve the Airbyte-managed OAuth secretId flow rather than replacing it with a personal access token, client ID, and client secret.

Must identify the established API requirement: source creation with secretId succeeds when credentials.auth_type is set to Client, despite that requirement not being documented in the referenced create-source documentation.

Must identify the established UI recovery: retrying the same authentication and source setup in a different browser or incognito session succeeds; it must not invent an unconfirmed browser-cache or connector-migration mechanism.
Must ground the answer in the collected evidence that existing connections continued running while edited and newly created managed-auth sources failed on both the Cloud UI and API paths.
Must not refer the reporter to Facebook Support as the resolution or attribute the problem solely to the Facebook account or account ID; that direction was contradicted by the reporter's evidence.
Must have the reporter verify successful source creation and Test and Save on the applicable UI and API paths before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Airbyte Cloud and API user who understands three-legged OAuth and can construct curl requests, inspect existing source configurations, share Cloud resource links, and record private reproduction videos, but has no visibility into Airbyte's internal credential handling.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, detailed, and cooperative; carefully distinguishes managed secretId authentication from manually supplied OAuth credentials, supplies concrete reproductions, and proactively reports a self-discovered resolution.
